issues.description: The problem statement and the template declare the Developer.monthsOfSwiftExperience property as an optional Int (Int?), but the solution implementation uses an optional Double (Double?). This is a type mismatch for a core attribute the exercise asks students to implement and use (e.g., in optional binding, a switch on 1, and increments when attending a course). Students following the problem and template will implement monthsOfSwiftExperience as Int?, while the solution shows a different type; this inconsistency can cause confusion when comparing implementations and may hide/alter intended behavior (e.g., wording about "months" implies integer months).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the Developer.monthsOfSwiftExperience type consistent across artifacts. Preferably align the solution with the problem/template by changing the solution's monthsOfSwiftExperience from Double? to Int? and update the initializer signature and any arithmetic accordingly (e.g., use Int arithmetic: monthsOfSwiftExperience = monthsOfSwiftExperience + 1). This preserves the intended semantic of "months" being integer values and removes student confusion when comparing template, spec, and reference solution.
